sections.subtitle: Dalmatinac na solarni pogon: Tonino Picula u Čušpajzu
sections.screenshot_description: Tonino Picula u studiju podcasta Čušpajz pozdravlja voditelja i šali se da kao Dalmatinac radi na solarni pogon
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **Čušpajz** otvara se svečanim predstavljanjem. Voditelj gosta najavljuje kao zastupnika u Hrvatskom saboru, zastupnika u Europskom parlamentu i, kako kaže, **„zvijezdu Europskog parlamenta za Srbiju“**. Riječ je o **Toninu Piculi**, političaru koji u Europskom parlamentu obnaša ulogu stalnog izvjestitelja za odnose sa Srbijom, pa se razgovor gotovo neizbježno otvara upravo temom koja ovih dana puni naslovnice.

Na pitanje kako je, Picula odgovara s dozom humora: lijep je dan, a on je Dalmatinac koji **„radi na solarni pogon“**, pa se osjeća dobro. Posla je, priznaje, puno, ali takav je ritam. Nakon kratkog upoznavanja voditelj odmah prelazi na najaktualniju temu, o kojoj je Picula proteklih dana dao niz izjava: izbore u Srbiji.
sections.subtitle_en: Solar-powered Dalmatian: Tonino Picula in Čušpajz
sections.screenshot_description_en: Tonino Picula in the Čušpajz podcast studio greets the host and jokes that as a Dalmatian he is solar-powered
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the podcast **Čušpajz** opens with a ceremonial introduction. The host announces the guest as a member of the Croatian Parliament, a member of the European Parliament, and, as he says, the **"star of the European Parliament for Serbia"**. This refers to **Tonino Picula**, a politician who serves in the European Parliament as the standing rapporteur for relations with Serbia, so the conversation almost inevitably opens with the very topic that has been making headlines these days.

Asked how he is doing, Picula responds with a dose of humor: it is a nice day, and he is a Dalmatian who **"runs on solar power"**, so he feels good. There is, he admits, a lot of work, but such is the pace. After a brief getting-to-know-you, the host immediately moves on to the most topical subject, about which Picula has made a series of statements in recent days: the elections in Serbia.

sections.subtitle: Plebiscit protiv autokracije: kako su studenti srušili Vučića na glasačkim kutijama
sections.screenshot_description: Picula objašnjava plebiscitarnu pobjedu studentske liste i razliku od pola milijuna glasova
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da su izbori u Srbiji u medijima opisivani kao **referendum protiv Vučića** i pita gosta je li očekivao tako uvjerljivu razliku. Picula odgovara da ga smjer događaja nije iznenadio, osobito u posljednjih nekoliko mjeseci, kada je postalo jasno da je studentska lista **politički sazrela** i obavila dobre, pa i tehničke pripreme za izbore.

Kao ključnu ističe **„generalnu probu“** održanu šest mjeseci ranije, kada su se u deset mjesta i gradova u Srbiji održali lokalni izbori. Vučić je u tim sredinama tada pobijedio, ali je, prema Piculinoj procjeni, iskustvo tog nastupa studentima znatno pomoglo da procijene što trebaju napraviti kako bi uspjeli na općim izborima za srpski parlament.

Trendovi su bili na strani studenata, no, kaže Picula, nitko nije mogao predvidjeti ovako **plebiscitarnu pobjedu** od **pola milijuna glasova razlike**, i to u uvjetima koji nisu išli na ruku ni ranijim oporbenim strankama ni studentskoj listi. Vučić je, naglašava, poznat po vrlo vještoj manipulaciji, pa i falsificiranju izbora. Ipak, u Srbiji se dogodila svojevrsna **društvena prekretnica**, a nezapamćeno visok odaziv pokazao je da je zemlja 14 godina polako sazrijevala za trenutak kada će na dan **25. listopada** glasačkim kutijama biti pogođena jedna autokracija.

Sve to, objašnjava gost, ne bi bilo moguće bez političkog buđenja dotad prilično uspavanog dijela društva: **studenata, pa i srednjoškolaca**, koji su se pobunili protiv raširene korupcije koja je, kako sami kažu, **počela i ubijati**. Picula podsjeća na tragediju u **Novom Sadu**, gdje je u padu nadstrešnice živote izgubilo 16 ljudi. Aktivizam koji je u početku djelovao spontano, ali i pomalo difuzno, doveo je do toga da Vučić na vlasti nije dočekao drugu obljetnicu novosadske tragedije. Picula to opisuje kao **eksperiment u političkom organiziranju** koji autokracija, unatoč svim mehanizmima pa i brutalnosti, nije uspjela poništiti. Vučić je tako poslan u oporbu.
sections.subtitle_en: Plebiscite against autocracy: how students brought down Vučić at the ballot boxes
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula explains the plebiscitary victory of the student list and the difference of half a million votes
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that the elections in Serbia were described in the media as a **referendum against Vučić** and asks the guest whether he expected such a convincing margin. Picula answers that the direction of events did not surprise him, especially in the last few months, when it became clear that the student list had **matured politically** and carried out good, and even technical, preparations for the elections.

As key he highlights the **"dress rehearsal"** held six months earlier, when local elections were held in ten towns and cities in Serbia. Vučić won in those communities then, but, according to Picula's assessment, the experience of that performance significantly helped the students assess what they needed to do in order to succeed in the general elections for the Serbian parliament.

The trends were on the side of the students, but, Picula says, no one could have predicted such a **plebiscitary victory** by **half a million votes difference**, and that under conditions that did not favor either the previous opposition parties or the student list. Vučić, he emphasizes, is known for very skillful manipulation, and even the falsification of elections. Nevertheless, a kind of **social turning point** occurred in Serbia, and the unprecedentedly high turnout showed that the country had been slowly maturing for 14 years for the moment when on the day of **October 25** an autocracy would be struck by ballot boxes.

All of this, the guest explains, would not have been possible without the political awakening of a hitherto rather dormant part of society: **students, and even high schoolers**, who rebelled against widespread corruption that, as they themselves say, **began killing too**. Picula recalls the tragedy in **Novi Sad**, where 16 people lost their lives in the collapse of the canopy. Activism that at the beginning seemed spontaneous, but also somewhat diffuse, led to Vučić not seeing the second anniversary of the Novi Sad tragedy in power. Picula describes this as an **experiment in political organizing** that the autocracy, despite all mechanisms and even brutality, failed to undo. Vučić was thus sent into opposition.

sections.subtitle: Brzo priznanje poraza i plan B: opstrukcija preko „duboke države“
sections.screenshot_description: Picula opisuje paravojne skupine i žandarmeriju na ulicama Beograda u izbornoj noći
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da je Vučić neuobičajeno brzo priznao poraz, navodno na temelju izlaznih anketa, i pita krije li se iza toga možda plan za nerede. Picula pojašnjava da su **izlazne ankete u Srbiji zabranjene**, ali da je Vučić sigurno imao svoje ljude na gotovo svakom od **više od 8.300 biračkih mjesta**. Zato je vjerojatno bio prvi u Srbiji koji je dobio pouzdane podatke o ishodu izbora i morao je vrlo brzo donijeti odluku.

Prema Piculinoj procjeni, Vučić je **odustao od plana da provociranim neredima poništi izbornu volju naroda**. Sat-dva prije nego što je izašao pred novinare, na ulicama su se ponovno pojavile njegove paravojne skupine, takozvani „ćaci“ iz notornog „ćacilenda“, a na ulicama Beograda viđena je i **žandarmerija**, koja, kako ističe gost, prije svega služi obračunu s prosvjednicima. Sve je, dakle, bilo pripremljeno za scenarij u kojem bi se nakon nekog isprovociranog incidenta pokušalo poništiti izbore. No s obzirom na golemu razliku u glasovima, Vučić je procijenio da bi si tako skratio političku karijeru, **„a možda i nešto drugo“**.

Umjesto toga, prema Piculi, odlučio je priznati poraz, ali iz skupštinskih klupa nastaviti djelovati uz pomoć onoga što sam pripisuje drugima: **duboke države**, koju je, kaže gost, gradio 14 godina. Cilj mu je na svaki način **opstruirati novu vlast** i pričekati da se ona istroši, zbog neiskustva, ali i zbog izrazite heterogenosti **140 zastupnika** studentske liste koji su ušli u skupštinu, kako bi zatim povratio boju u lice i možda se vratio na vlast.

Picula zato upozorava: **Vučića se nipošto ne smije podcjenjivati**. Nova vlast, izabrana s ovolikim entuzijazmom, nema vremena za gubljenje, jer će svako odugovlačenje jačati samo Vučića.
sections.subtitle_en: Quick concession of defeat and plan B: obstruction via the "deep state"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula describes paramilitary groups and the gendarmerie on the streets of Belgrade on election night
sections.content_en:
The host notes that Vučić conceded defeat unusually quickly, allegedly based on exit polls, and asks whether a plan for riots might be hidden behind this. Picula explains that **exit polls are banned in Serbia**, but that Vučić certainly had his people at almost every one of the **more than 8,300 polling stations**. Therefore, he was probably the first in Serbia to receive reliable data on the outcome of the election and had to make a decision very quickly.

According to Picula's assessment, Vučić **abandoned the plan to annul the electoral will of the people through provoked riots**. An hour or two before he stepped in front of journalists, his paramilitary groups, the so-called "ćaci" from the notorious "ćaciland", reappeared on the streets, and the **gendarmerie** was also seen on the streets of Belgrade, which, as the guest points out, primarily serves to clash with protesters. Everything was, therefore, prepared for a scenario in which, after some provoked incident, an attempt would be made to annul the elections. But given the huge difference in votes, Vučić assessed that he would thus shorten his political career, **"and perhaps something else as well"**.

Instead, according to Picula, he decided to concede defeat, but to continue acting from the parliamentary benches with the help of what he himself attributes to others: the **deep state**, which, the guest says, he built for 14 years. His goal is to **obstruct the new government** in every way and wait for it to wear itself out, due to inexperience, but also due to the extreme heterogeneity of the **140 deputies** of the student list who entered parliament, in order to then regain color in his face and perhaps return to power.

Picula therefore warns: **Vučić must by no means be underestimated**. The new government, elected with so much enthusiasm, has no time to lose, because any delay will only strengthen Vučić.

sections.subtitle: Tajnovitost kao strategija: što se zapravo zna o studentskoj listi
sections.screenshot_description: Picula govori o studentskim plenumima na fakultetima na kojima su se donosile ključne odluke
sections.content:
Voditelj ističe da se u Hrvatskoj o studentskoj listi pisalo relativno malo, uz nagađanja da je riječ o **projektu stranih centara moći**, te da do izborne noći nisu bila poznata ni imena kandidata za ključne funkcije. Društvene mreže i mediji, dodaje, preplavljeni su svakakvim isječcima i klipovima.

Picula odgovara da to nije čudno, jer su se **studenti sami pobrinuli da se o njima zna što manje**. Cijelo su vrijeme uspjeli sačuvati autonomiju djelovanja, a s njihovih **famoznih plenuma** na fakultetima i sveučilištima diljem Srbije gotovo ništa nije iscurilo. Upravo su se na plenumima donosile sve krupne odluke:

- kako organizirati prosvjede,
- kako postaviti logistiku prosvjeda koji su trajali gotovo dvije godine,
- kako djelovati na lokalnom terenu,
- prema kojim kriterijima birati ljude koje će staviti na izborne liste.

Notorni tabloidi mogli su samo nagađati, a studentske redove očito nije uspjela probiti ni **Bezbednosno-informativna agencija**, koja, napominje Picula, nije baš nesposobna služba. Riječ je o eksperimentalnom načinu djelovanja kojemu je cilj bio zaštititi upravo taj **modus operandi**. Ako se o studentima nije dovoljno znalo ni u samoj Srbiji, zaključuje, nije čudo da se o njima malo zna i u Hrvatskoj.

Sada se, međutim, stvari radikalno mijenjaju. Plenumi su se pokazali izuzetno učinkovitim mehanizmom rušenja agresivne, autoritarne vlasti koja je dominirala institucijama, ali otvara se novo pitanje: **kako odlučivanje u plenumima prenijeti u odlučivanje u institucijama vlasti**. Picula smatra da studentski pokret nakon trijumfa mora prijeći **iz faze tajnovitosti u fazu personifikacije**. Uskoro će se znati tko će biti premijer, tko ministri i tko će preuzeti odgovornost u agencijama, policiji i vojsci. Vjeruje da su studenti za to spremni i da se treba još malo strpjeti.
sections.subtitle_en: Secrecy as a strategy: what is actually known about the student list
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula speaks about student plenums at faculties where key decisions were made
sections.content_en:
The host points out that relatively little was written in Croatia about the student list, along with speculations that it was a **project of foreign power centers**, and that until election night not even the names of candidates for key positions were known. Social networks and the media, he adds, are flooded with all kinds of snippets and clips.

Picula responds that this is not surprising, because the **students themselves made sure that as little as possible was known about them**. The entire time they managed to preserve their autonomy of action, and from their **famous plenums** at faculties and universities across Serbia almost nothing leaked. It was precisely at the plenums that all major decisions were made:

- how to organize the protests,
- how to set up the logistics of the protests that lasted almost two years,
- how to operate on the local ground,
- according to what criteria to select the people they would put on the electoral lists.

Notorious tabloids could only guess, and the student ranks were apparently not breached even by the **Security Intelligence Agency**, which, Picula notes, is not exactly an incompetent service. This is an experimental way of operating whose goal was precisely to protect that **modus operandi**. If not enough was known about the students even in Serbia itself, he concludes, it is no wonder that little is known about them in Croatia as well.

Now, however, things are changing radically. The plenums proved to be an extremely effective mechanism for bringing down an aggressive, authoritarian government that dominated the institutions, but a new question opens up: **how to transfer plenum decision-making into decision-making in government institutions**. Picula believes that after its triumph, the student movement must transition **from the phase of secrecy to the phase of personification**. Soon it will be known who will be the prime minister, who the ministers, and who will take responsibility in agencies, the police, and the military. He believes that the students are ready for this and that one should be patient a little longer.

sections.subtitle: Profesori i sportaši umjesto političara: potpuni reset srbijanske scene
sections.screenshot_description: Picula ističe da Socijalistička partija Srbije prvi put od 1990. nije ušla u parlament
sections.content:
Na pitanje što misli o imenima budućih dužnosnika koja se pojavljuju u medijima, Picula odgovara da je riječ o ljudima koji su u užem smislu **politički neiskusni**. Nisu obnašali nikakvu bitniju političku funkciju, pa ih nitko nije imao prilike sresti u konferencijskoj dvorani, na bilateralnom susretu ili na nekom panelu. Radi se o **sveučilišnim profesorima i ljudima iz svijeta sporta**, pa je o njihovim političkim kapacitetima zasad teško govoriti. Ono što je sigurno jest da su zadobili povjerenje studenata, koji su pokazali veliku nepovjerljivost prema srpskoj oporbi i cijelo vrijeme odbijali suradnju s klasičnim strankama.

Picula pritom naglašava jednu važnu činjenicu: studentska lista nije samo poslala u oporbu svemoćnog, „sa ili bez navodnika“, Aleksandra Vučića, nego je **praktički uništila i dotadašnju oporbu** iz posljednjeg saziva Narodne skupštine. Među poraženima su i snažne, etablirane organizacije poput **Miloševićeve Socijalističke partije Srbije**, koja **prvi put nakon 1990. nije ušla u parlament**. Isto se dogodilo i nekim drugim etabliranim strankama.

Riječ je, zaključuje gost, o **kompletnom resetu srbijanske političke scene**, na kojoj sada praktički postoji dvostranačje. Ipak, procjenjuje da ni studentska lista ni Vučićeva stranka, koja je osvojila oko **103 do 104 mandata**, u idućih pola godine neće ostati u sadašnjem obliku. Okolnosti, pritisci i problemi koje treba rješavati, smatra, itekako će utjecati na njihov konačan oblik i veličinu.
sections.subtitle_en: Professors and athletes instead of politicians: a complete reset of the Serbian scene
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula points out that the Socialist Party of Serbia did not enter parliament for the first time since 1990
sections.content_en:
When asked what he thinks about the names of future officials appearing in the media, Picula answers that these are people who in the narrower sense are **politically inexperienced**. They have not held any significant political office, so no one has had the opportunity to meet them in a conference hall, at a bilateral meeting, or on a panel. They are **university professors and people from the world of sports**, so it is difficult for now to speak about their political capacities. What is certain is that they have gained the trust of the students, who showed great distrust toward the Serbian opposition and refused cooperation with traditional parties the entire time.

At the same time, Picula emphasizes one important fact: the student list not only sent the all-powerful, "with or without quotation marks", Aleksandar Vučić into opposition, but **practically destroyed the previous opposition as well** from the last convocation of the National Assembly. Among the defeated are strong, established organizations such as **Milošević's Socialist Party of Serbia**, which **did not enter parliament for the first time since 1990**. The same happened to some other established parties.

This is, the guest concludes, a **complete reset of the Serbian political scene**, where there is now practically a two-party system. Nevertheless, he estimates that neither the student list nor Vučić's party, which won about **103 to 104 seats**, will remain in their present form in the next six months. Circumstances, pressures, and problems that need to be solved, he believes, will significantly influence their final shape and size.

sections.subtitle: Upad u Informat i dva testa za novu vlast
sections.screenshot_description: Picula nabraja dva testa koja studentska lista mora proći na vlasti
sections.content:
Voditelj upozorava na scene **upada u televiziju Informat** te na snimke na kojima prosvjednici ulaze u općine kod pojedinih načelnika. Razumije studente, kaže, jer je Informat bio kakav je bio, ali smatra da bi nova vlast takve stvari morala hitno riješiti, inače riskira gubitak povjerenja građana, Europe i susjeda.

Picula se slaže. Za čovjeka na čelu Informata, kaže, „zaista se nije žaliti“ jer je nanio mnogo zla, i nije bio jedini. No studentska lista i ljudi koji će u njezino ime obnašati vlast morat će proći **barem dva testa**:

- **Test načina vladanja**: kako preuzeti i obnašati vlast tako da to bude **potpuno drugačije** od načina na koji su to radili Aleksandar Vučić i njegovi.
- **Test odlučnosti**: odmah se uhvatiti ukoštac s gorućim problemima srpskog društva i politike, koji su zemlju **14 godina držali na mjestu**.

Upravo je nerješavanje tih problema, ističe Picula, dovelo do toga da Srbija, zemlja s respektabilnom tradicijom državnosti i snažnom administracijom, na putu prema Europskoj uniji **zaostane čak i za Albanijom**. O Crnoj Gori da i ne govori, a dodaje da su i **Ukrajina i Moldavija** na putu da se plasiraju puno bolje. S tim se problemima nova vlast mora suočiti odmah, „praktički jučer“.
sections.subtitle_en: Break-in at Informat and two tests for the new government
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula lists two tests that the student list must pass in power
sections.content_en:
The host warns about the scenes of the **break-in at television Informat** and footage showing protesters entering municipalities to see certain mayors. He understands the students, he says, because Informat was what it was, but he believes that the new government should resolve such things urgently, otherwise it risks losing the trust of citizens, Europe, and neighbors.

Picula agrees. For the man at the head of Informat, he says, "there is really nothing to pity" because he caused a lot of evil, and he was not the only one. But the student list and the people who will govern in its name will have to pass **at least two tests**:

- **Test of the manner of governance**: how to take over and exercise power so that it is **completely different** from the way Aleksandar Vučić and his associates did it.
- **Test of determination**: to immediately grapple with the burning problems of Serbian society and politics, which **kept the country in place for 14 years**.

It is precisely the failure to resolve these problems, Picula points out, that led to Serbia, a country with a respectable tradition of statehood and strong administration, **lagging even behind Albania** on the path toward the European Union. Not to mention Montenegro, and he adds that both **Ukraine and Moldova** are on track to place much better. The new government must confront these problems immediately, "practically yesterday".

sections.subtitle: Politički adrenalin: mladost kao snaga i slabost
sections.screenshot_description: Picula govori o političkom adrenalinu mladih ljudi koji su srušili naizgled svemoćnu vlast
sections.content:
Voditelj se pita jesu li novi akteri uopće svjesni koliko je posla pred njima. Picula smatra da su trenutačno **pod političkim adrenalinom**: kada se na neortodoksan način sruši vlast koja je djelovala svemoćno, čovjek doista pomisli da je **„samo nebo granica“**.

Ne treba im to zamjeriti, dodaje. Na ulicama Beograda i drugih srbijanskih gradova uglavnom su bili **mladi ljudi**, a od ljudi u dvadesetima bilo bi možda i nepravedno očekivati veliko političko iskustvo i poznavanje cijelog mehanizma vlasti. No zaključuje da će **morati brzo učiti**.
sections.subtitle_en: Political adrenaline: youth as strength and weakness
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula speaks about the political adrenaline of young people who brought down a seemingly omnipotent government
sections.content_en:
The host wonders whether the new actors are even aware of how much work lies ahead of them. Picula believes they are currently **under political adrenaline**: when a government that seemed omnipotent is brought down in an unorthodox way, one truly thinks that **"the sky is the only limit"**.

They should not be blamed for that, he adds. On the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian cities there were mostly **young people**, and from people in their twenties it would perhaps be unfair to expect great political experience and knowledge of the entire mechanism of power. But he concludes that **they will have to learn quickly**.

sections.subtitle: Kraj destabilizacije susjeda? Kosovo, BiH i Crna Gora u Vučićevoj sjeni
sections.screenshot_description: Picula podsjeća na upad paravojnih snaga u selo Banjsku na sjeveru Kosova
sections.content:
Voditelj postavlja optimističan scenarij: ako nova vlast krene kako treba, to bi moglo **ubrzati europske integracije u cijeloj regiji**, od Bosne i Hercegovine do Crne Gore i Kosova. Picula se slaže, uz napomenu da Srbija zbog svoje veličine i utjecaja **nije drugorazredna zemlja na Zapadnom Balkanu** i doista može utjecati na događaje u susjedstvu, što je Vučić, kaže, zloupotrebljavao.

U proteklih 14 godina Vučić je, prema Piculi, prije svega **destabilizirao političke prilike** u susjednim zemljama. Kao primjere navodi:

- **Upad paravojnih snaga u selo Banjsku** na sjeveru Kosova, u kojem je bilo i smrtnih slučajeva. Radojčić, koji je preuzeo odgovornost za taj upad, pojavljivao se na skupovima SNS-a tijekom ove kampanje, što Picula vidi kao dokaz da je upad sponzorirala Vučićeva vlast.
- **Odnose s Miloradom Dodikom**, kojeg naziva „wannabe razbijačem Bosne i Hercegovine“, koji je pravno i politički sankcioniran.
- **Pokušaje utjecaja na europski put i državnost Crne Gore.** Crna Gora ove je godine obilježila 20 godina obnove državnosti, na što je Vučić reagirao bijesno, kao da je Crna Gora oteta Srbiji, a učinio je sve da je veže uz sebe i tako joj oteža ulazak u Europsku uniju.

Pomak se, smatra Picula, mora osjetiti odmah: nova vlast za početak sigurno neće proizvoditi incidente u susjednim zemljama i trebala bi otvoriti mogućnost **punog partnerstva**, od kojeg će najviše koristi imati upravo Srbija. To neće biti jednostavno, ali ga početni narativi ljudi koji će obnašati funkcije u novoj vlasti ohrabruju.
sections.subtitle_en: End of destabilization of neighbors? Kosovo, BiH, and Montenegro in Vučić's shadow
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula recalls the incursion of paramilitary forces into the village of Banjska in northern Kosovo
sections.content_en:
The host presents an optimistic scenario: if the new government starts off as it should, that could **accelerate European integration in the entire region**, from Bosnia and Herzegovina to Montenegro and Kosovo. Picula agrees, with the note that Serbia, due to its size and influence, **is not a second-rate country in the Western Balkans** and can truly influence events in the neighborhood, which Vučić, he says, abused.

In the past 14 years, according to Picula, Vučić primarily **destabilized political conditions** in neighboring countries. As examples he cites:

- **The incursion of paramilitary forces into the village of Banjska** in northern Kosovo, in which there were fatalities. Radojčić, who claimed responsibility for that incursion, appeared at SNS rallies during this campaign, which Picula sees as proof that the incursion was sponsored by Vučić's government.
- **Relations with Milorad Dodik**, whom he calls a "wannabe wrecker of Bosnia and Herzegovina", who has been legally and politically sanctioned.
- **Attempts to influence the European path and statehood of Montenegro.** Montenegro this year marked 20 years of the restoration of statehood, to which Vučić reacted furiously, as if Montenegro had been stolen from Serbia, and did everything to tie it to himself and thus make its entry into the European Union more difficult.

A shift, Picula believes, must be felt immediately: for starters, the new government certainly will not produce incidents in neighboring countries and should open the possibility of a **full partnership**, from which Serbia itself will benefit the most. That will not be simple, but the initial narratives of the people who will hold offices in the new government encourage him.

sections.subtitle: Dodik nije politički mrtav: skenirani glasovi i američki lobisti
sections.screenshot_description: Picula objašnjava novi izborni sustav u BiH koji je pokazao stvarni broj birača
sections.content:
Voditelj vraća razgovor na Bosnu i Hercegovinu i Republiku Srpsku: Dodik je u nezavidnom položaju, ali ga je **Trump pomilovao** i vratio u politički život. Picula, koji je i sam bio prisutan na izborima u BiH, ocjenjuje ih **dobro organiziranima**, i to po novom sustavu koji je onemogućio da, kako slikovito kaže, glasa „pokojni babo“.

Prvi put u povijesti dejtonske BiH evidentiran je **stvarni broj birača**: umjesto nekih tri milijuna i nešto, sada je jasno da je riječ o **jedva oko 2,2 milijuna ljudi**. Izbori su provedeni po relativno kompliciranom postupku, uz **skeniranje glasačkih listića** prije nego što padnu u kutiju, a rezultat nitko nije osporavao, ni pobjednici ni gubitnici.

To je, nažalost, legitimiralo i Milorada Dodika, čiji je **SNSD trijumfirao u Republici Srpskoj**, što potvrđuje da Dodik nije politički mrtav. Jedan od razloga, slaže se Picula s voditeljem, jest **uspješno lobiranje u SAD-u**. Postoje naznake da je Dodik potrošio ozbiljan novac kod američkih lobističkih kuća bliskih Trumpovoj administraciji kako bi ga skinuli s crne liste, što je uspjelo. Vučiću to, primjećuje gost, nije uspjelo, bez obzira na to koliko novca troši u SAD-u.

To je dobra vijest samo za Dodika i za one koji sanjaju o Bosni i Hercegovini koja ne postoji ili je vrlo slaba, ali nije dobra vijest za samu BiH. Ipak, Picula vjeruje da će prostor za Dodikovo djelovanje biti **znatno omeđeniji** i da su njegovi „zlatni dani“ iza njega.
sections.subtitle_en: Dodik is not politically dead: scanned votes and American lobbyists
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula explains the new electoral system in BiH that showed the real number of voters
sections.content_en:
The host returns the conversation to Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska: Dodik is in an unenviable position, but **Trump pardoned him** and returned him to political life. Picula, who was himself present at the elections in BiH, assesses them as **well-organized**, under a new system that prevented, as he colorfully says, the "deceased babo" from voting.

For the first time in the history of Dayton BiH, the **real number of voters** was recorded: instead of some three million-odd, it is now clear that it is **barely around 2.2 million people**. The elections were conducted according to a relatively complicated procedure, with the **scanning of ballots** before they drop into the box, and no one disputed the result, neither the winners nor the losers.

This, unfortunately, also legitimized Milorad Dodik, whose **SNSD triumphed in Republika Srpska**, confirming that Dodik is not politically dead. One of the reasons, Picula agrees with the host, is **successful lobbying in the USA**. There are indications that Dodik spent serious money with American lobbying firms close to the Trump administration to get him off the blacklist, which succeeded. Vučić, the guest observes, did not succeed in that, regardless of how much money he spends in the USA.

This is good news only for Dodik and for those who dream of a Bosnia and Herzegovina that does not exist or is very weak, but it is not good news for BiH itself. Nevertheless, Picula believes that the space for Dodik's maneuvering will be **significantly more bounded** and that his "golden days" are behind him.

sections.subtitle: Beograd 2016.: susret koji je Vučić zapamtio
sections.screenshot_description: Picula prepričava kako je Vučiću pred članovima odbora Europskog parlamenta uzvratio na napad na Hrvatsku
sections.content:
Prije zatvaranja poglavlja o Vučiću, voditelj pita gosta je li ga osobno sreo. Picula otkriva da ga je sreo **prvi i jedini put 2016. godine**, kada je u Beograd došao u sklopu **Vanjskopolitičkog odbora Europskog parlamenta**. Tijekom službenih razgovora, u prisutnosti 15-ak do 20 članova odbora, Vučić si je dopustio **brutalan napad na Republiku Hrvatsku**, optužujući je za „sve i svašta“, od ustaštva do progona Srba.

Picula je tada, kako kaže, digao ruku i pred svima mu rekao da **o fašizmu ne može govoriti netko tko ima jasne fašističke epizode u životu**. Vučić je to zapamtio i nakon toga izbjegavao svaki susret s njim.

Kada se voditelj našali da je Picula tako postao *persona non grata*, gost objašnjava da ga je Vučićev narativ blatio, kao i cijeli niz ljudi koji režimu nisu bili po volji. Vučić je, međutim, osobito teško primio njegovo **imenovanje za stalnog izvjestitelja Europskog parlamenta za odnose sa Srbijom**. Već dan uoči imenovanja tabloidi su proradili i nisu prestali proizvoditi laži i optužbe praktički do jučer. Picula poručuje da se on nije promijenio: prosudbe donosi na temelju argumenata, uvida i činjenica, i nada se da se otvara nova stranica.
sections.subtitle_en: Belgrade 2016: an encounter Vučić remembered
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula recounts how he pushed back against Vučić's attack on Croatia in front of members of the European Parliament committee
sections.content_en:
Before closing the chapter on Vučić, the host asks the guest whether he had met him personally. Picula reveals that he met him for the **first and only time in 2016**, when he arrived in Belgrade as part of the **Foreign Affairs Committee of the European Parliament**. During official talks, in the presence of 15 to 20 committee members, Vučić allowed himself a **brutal attack on the Republic of Croatia**, accusing it of "all kinds of things", from Ustašism to the persecution of Serbs.

Picula then, as he says, raised his hand and told him in front of everyone that **someone who has clear fascist episodes in their life cannot speak about fascism**. Vučić remembered that and after that avoided every encounter with him.

When the host jokes that Picula thus became a *persona non grata*, the guest explains that Vučić's narrative smeared him, as well as a whole series of people who were not to the regime's liking. Vučić, however, took particularly hard his **appointment as the standing rapporteur of the European Parliament for relations with Serbia**. Already the day before the appointment, the tabloids started up and did not stop producing lies and accusations practically until yesterday. Picula says that he has not changed: he makes judgments based on arguments, insights, and facts, and hopes that a new page is turning.

sections.subtitle: Nestali, odšteta i arhivi: istina je udaljena samo za dobru volju
sections.screenshot_description: Picula govori o arhivima u Beogradu i potrazi za nestalima iz Domovinskog rata
sections.content:
Voditelj ističe da hrvatsku javnost i danas zanimaju **ratna odšteta** od Srbije i **pronalazak nestalih**, kojih navodi 1.725. Picula se slaže i naglašava da je dosad postojala **opstrukcija**. Ako nova vlast želi pokazati kvalitativnu razliku u odnosu na „predugih 14 godina“ Vučićeve vladavine, morat će napraviti iskorake.

Ohrabruje ga, kaže, što je **gospodin Stojanović** izjavio da se **srami Vučićeva narativa o devedesetima**. Sada je prilika da se od te politike napravi stvarni odmak, prije svega boljom suradnjom na utvrđivanju istine o **nestalima u Domovinskom ratu**. Arhivi su, ističe, u Beogradu, a između istine i onoga što hrvatska strana želi stoji samo **dobra volja da se ti arhivi otvore**.
sections.subtitle_en: Missing persons, compensation, and archives: the truth is separated only by good will
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula talks about the archives in Belgrade and the search for those missing from the Homeland War
sections.content_en:
The host points out that the Croatian public is still interested in **war compensation** from Serbia and **finding the missing**, of whom he cites 1,725. Picula agrees and emphasizes that until now there has been **obstruction**. If the new government wants to show a qualitative difference compared to the "overly long 14 years" of Vučić's rule, it will have to make strides forward.

He is encouraged, he says, by **Mr. Stojanović's** statement that he is **ashamed of Vučić's narrative about the nineties**. Now is the opportunity to make a real departure from that policy, primarily through better cooperation in establishing the truth about the **missing in the Homeland War**. The archives are, he emphasizes, in Belgrade, and between the truth and what the Croatian side wants stands only the **good will to open those archives**.

sections.subtitle: Nije dovoljna verbalna distanca: činjenice o devedesetima nisu stvar interpretacije
sections.screenshot_description: Picula naglašava da su činjenice o devedesetima utvrđene na međunarodnim sudovima
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je Picula bio oštar kritičar ne samo Vučićeva režima nego i **blage politike Europske unije** prema njemu, dok je Vučić „plesao“ s Rusijom, Kinom i Bruxellesom. Što ako studentska lista nastavi istim smjerom?

Picula se nada da neće. Promjene u Srbiji dočekane su s olakšanjem, uz nadu da nije smijenjena samo stara vlast, nego da će se napustiti i **ideološke pretpostavke Vučićeve vladavine**. Studenti su, uostalom, izbore dobili jasnim distanciranjem od Vučića kao, Piculinim riječima, **„patrijarha kriminala i korupcije“** čija je država imala samo demokratsku fasadu, a funkcionirala je po **mafijaškom sustavu**.

To, međutim, neće biti dovoljno da Srbija živi u miru sa susjedima i ostvari europske ambicije. **Verbalna distanca od devedesetih nije dovoljna**: politikom se mora pokazati koliko je Srbija svjesna svoje odgovornosti za te događaje. Ne može se, kaže, skrivati iza opće konstatacije da će se interpretacije uvijek razlikovati, pa da je za jedne riječ o agresiji, a za druge o pokušaju oružane secesije. **„Istina je istina. Činjenice su činjenice.“** One su, naglašava, utvrđene i na međunarodnim sudovima.

Picula priznaje da Hrvatska možda neće biti zadovoljna brzinom promjena, jer pobjednici očito imaju drugačije prioritete, pa u početku treba biti strpljiv. Na voditeljevu primjedbu da će se smjer vidjeti nakon sto dana, gost odgovara da si nova vlast **ne može dopustiti ni tih sto dana**, nego mora djelovati vrlo brzo.
sections.subtitle_en: Verbal distance is not enough: facts about the nineties are not a matter of interpretation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula emphasizes that the facts about the nineties were established in international courts
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that Picula was a sharp critic not only of Vučić's regime but also of the **mild policy of the European Union** toward him, while Vučić was "dancing" with Russia, China, and Brussels. What if the student list continues in the same direction?

Picula hopes they will not. Changes in Serbia were greeted with relief, with the hope that not only was the old government removed, but that the **ideological premises of Vučić's rule** will be abandoned as well. After all, the students won the elections by clearly distancing themselves from Vučić as, in Picula's words, the **"patriarch of crime and corruption"** whose state had only a democratic facade, while functioning according to a **mafia system**.

That, however, will not be enough for Serbia to live in peace with its neighbors and achieve European ambitions. **Verbal distance from the nineties is not enough**: policy must show how much Serbia is aware of its responsibility for those events. One cannot, he says, hide behind the general statement that interpretations will always differ, so that for some it is a matter of aggression, and for others an attempt at armed secession. **"Truth is truth. Facts are facts."** They were, he emphasizes, established in international courts as well.

Picula admits that Croatia may not be satisfied with the speed of changes, because the winners clearly have different priorities, so at the beginning one should be patient. To the host's remark that the direction will be seen after a hundred days, the guest replies that the new government **cannot afford even those hundred days**, but must act very quickly.

sections.subtitle: Nemiri u Francuskoj, Italiji i Belgiji: sociolog protiv pojednostavljivanja
sections.screenshot_description: Picula kao profesor sociologije analizira uzroke nemira u europskim državama
sections.content:
Razgovor se seli na zapad Europe. Voditelj spominje nerede u **Francuskoj, Italiji i Belgiji**, predstavljane kao studentske nemire, iza kojih se, prema njegovim riječima, krije velik broj legalnih i ilegalnih migranata. Navodi da je **Meloni poslala vojsku na ulice Milana**, da je u Francuskoj uveden policijski sat te da se na snimkama vide naoružani civili koji brane svoje trgovine. Pita je li to budućnost Europe.

Picula, i sam **profesor sociologije**, kaže da se pri traženju odgovora na politički fenomen najprije konzultira „sa sociologom u sebi“, a tek onda pusti političara Tonina Piculu da nešto kaže. Upozorava da treba izbjeći **političko pojednostavljivanje**: nemiri se događaju u državama članicama u kojima su na vlasti **različite političke opcije**, od Italije i Francuske do Španjolske, Njemačke i Belgije. Ono što ih povezuje jest **nezadovoljstvo građana**.

Uzrok vidi u **nagomilanoj frustraciji** društvenih slojeva koji u današnjoj Europskoj uniji gube osjećaj perspektive. Kao moguće izvore nabraja:

- **stambeno pitanje**, koje se pojavilo prije desetak-dvanaest godina, zaoštrilo se i osjeća se i u Hrvatskoj,
- **slabljenje srednjeg sloja** suočenog s digitalizacijom i gubitkom radnih mjesta,
- **školstvo i zdravstvo**, veliki javni izdaci koji prvi stradaju kod proračunske štednje,
- **strah za starost i mirovine**.

Sve se to često pripisuje migrantima, za što, smatra Picula, **nema izravnog opravdanja**. Podsjeća na podatak na koji je nedavno naišao: kako bi izgledalo hrvatsko gospodarstvo i BDP bez stranih radnika, među kojima su i radnici iz Srbije. A kamoli, dodaje, velika gospodarstva poput njemačkog, talijanskog, francuskog ili španjolskog.
sections.subtitle_en: Unrest in France, Italy, and Belgium: sociologist against oversimplification
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula as a sociology professor analyzes the causes of unrest in European countries
sections.content_en:
The conversation moves to western Europe. The host mentions riots in **France, Italy, and Belgium**, presented as student unrest, behind which, in his words, hides a large number of legal and illegal migrants. He states that **Meloni sent the army onto the streets of Milan**, that a curfew was introduced in France, and that armed civilians defending their shops are seen in videos. He asks if this is the future of Europe.

Picula, himself a **professor of sociology**, says that when seeking answers to a political phenomenon he first consults "the sociologist within himself", and only then lets the politician Tonino Picula say something. He warns that **political oversimplification** should be avoided: unrest is occurring in member states where **different political options** are in power, from Italy and France to Spain, Germany, and Belgium. What connects them is **citizen discontent**.

He sees the cause in the **accumulated frustration** of social strata that in today's European Union are losing a sense of perspective. As possible sources he lists:

- the **housing issue**, which emerged ten to twelve years ago, sharpened, and is felt in Croatia as well,
- the **weakening of the middle class** faced with digitalization and job losses,
- **education and healthcare**, large public expenditures that are the first to suffer during budget austerity,
- **fear for old age and pensions**.

All this is often attributed to migrants, for which, Picula believes, **there is no direct justification**. He recalls a data point he recently came across: what the Croatian economy and GDP would look like without foreign workers, among whom are workers from Serbia. Let alone, he adds, large economies like the German, Italian, French, or Spanish.

sections.subtitle: Tri megatrenda: sukobi, fragmentacija i svijet koji se vrti dvostruko brže
sections.screenshot_description: Picula nabraja tri megatrenda koji su promijenili svijet u posljednjih 15 godina
sections.content:
Svijet se, ističe Picula, u posljednjih 10 do 15 godina značajno promijenio, a on je uočio **tri megatrenda**:

- **Više sukoba, manje suradnje.** Slabe multilateralne organizacije u kojima se kolektivno dogovaralo.
- **Fragmentacija političke scene.** Sve je više novih igrača, pokreta i opcija, a tradicionalne stranke slabe. Kao ilustraciju navodi Europski parlament: prije desetak-petnaest godina dvije najjače grupacije, **EPP i Socijalisti i demokrati**, zajedno su imale oko 60 posto zastupnika, a danas jedva 40 posto. Ostatak su zauzeli oni koji su izabrani na valu nezadovoljstva sugrađana.
- **Akceleracija.** Sve se odvija nevjerojatno brzo, pa se, kaže, stječe dojam da se Zemlja okreće **dvostruko brže nego prije 20 godina**.

U takvim frustrirajućim vremenima, kada ljudi imaju osjećaj da institucije ne rade za njih, izlaze na ulice i traže promjene. Negdje kroz sindikalne štrajkove i političke pritiske, a negdje kroz masovne obračune s policijom, pa i s vojskom. Europska unija, zaključuje Picula, prolazi kroz **dosta turbulentno razdoblje**.
sections.subtitle_en: Three megatrends: conflicts, fragmentation, and a world spinning twice as fast
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula lists three megatrends that have changed the world in the last 15 years
sections.content_en:
The world, Picula points out, has significantly changed in the last 10 to 15 years, and he has observed **three megatrends**:

- **More conflict, less cooperation.** Multilateral organizations in which agreements were collectively made are weakening.
- **Fragmentation of the political scene.** There are increasingly more new players, movements, and options, while traditional parties are weakening. As an illustration he cites the European Parliament: ten to fifteen years ago the two strongest groupings, the **EPP and the Socialists and Democrats**, together held about 60 percent of MEPs, and today barely 40 percent. The rest was taken by those elected on the wave of their fellow citizens' dissatisfaction.
- **Acceleration.** Everything takes place incredibly quickly, so that, he says, one gets the impression that the Earth is spinning **twice as fast as 20 years ago**.

In such frustrating times, when people feel that institutions are not working for them, they take to the streets and demand changes. In some places through union strikes and political pressure, and in others through mass clashes with the police, and even with the army. The European Union, Picula concludes, is going through a **rather turbulent period**.

sections.subtitle: Zajednica država, a ne zajednička država: zašto Bruxelles odlučuje sporo
sections.screenshot_description: Picula prepričava šalu o 27 zastava ispred Europskog parlamenta u Strasbourgu
sections.content:
Europska unija, objašnjava Picula, ima svojevrsnu **„tvorničku postavku“** koja je razlikuje od Kine, Indije, Amerike, Argentine, Indonezije ili Rusije: ona **nije zajednička država, nego zajednica država**. Svaki dogovor zahtijeva poštivanje procedura koje znaju biti duge, a to često frustrira ljude jer se odgovori ne nalaze ni brzo ni jednostavno.

Picula prepričava šalu jednog prijatelja: **27 zastava ispred zgrade Europskog parlamenta u Strasbourgu u isti smjer može okrenuti samo vjetar**. Unatoč tome, smatra da je EU i dalje jedan od prostora na kojima se **najbolje živi na planetu**, s obzirom na razinu zaštite rada te socijalnih i zdravstvenih prava. Za Uniju se vrijedi boriti, ali ignorirati njezine probleme nije dobro.

Voditelj priznaje da i sam često kritizira briselsku administraciju: odluke se donose teško i dugo, građani su izgubili povjerenje, a dok se sukobi intenziviraju, iz Bruxellesa stižu odluke poput onih o digitalnoj gotovini, koje su ljudima zasad posve nebitne.

Picula uzvraća da se pritom zaboravljaju opipljive **tekovine EU-a**:

- **ukidanje roaminga**, pa se iz Lisabona može razgovarati s Karlovcem po cijeni kao da je riječ o Oslu,
- **slobodno putovanje**, pa se samo s osobnom iskaznicom bez problema može otići iz Karlovca u Stockholm ili Uppsalu,
- **zajednička valuta**, uz koju se odmah zna koliko što vrijedi.

EU je, kaže, **eksperiment koji traje do danas**. Nikada u povijesti europskog kontinenta toliko država nije bilo povezano bitnim elementima državnosti, i to na kontinentu na kojem su se stoljećima zbog političkih i vjerskih razlika „rezali vratovi“. Danas postoje nemiri i nezadovoljstvo, ali oni su legitimni i mogu se legitimno izraziti.
sections.subtitle_en: A community of states, not a common state: why Brussels decides slowly
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula recounts a joke about 27 flags in front of the European Parliament in Strasbourg
sections.content_en:
The European Union, Picula explains, has a kind of **"factory setting"** that distinguishes it from China, India, America, Argentina, Indonesia, or Russia: it is **not a common state, but a community of states**. Every agreement requires compliance with procedures that can be long, and this often frustrates people because answers are found neither quickly nor easily.

Picula recounts a friend's joke: **the 27 flags in front of the European Parliament building in Strasbourg can only be turned in the same direction by the wind**. Despite that, he believes that the EU is still one of the places where **life is best on the planet**, considering the level of labor protection as well as social and healthcare rights. The Union is worth fighting for, but ignoring its problems is not good.

The host admits that he himself often criticizes the Brussels administration: decisions are made with difficulty and take long, citizens have lost trust, and while conflicts intensify, decisions arrive from Brussels like those on digital cash, which are completely irrelevant to people for now.

Picula retorts that tangible **achievements of the EU** are forgotten in the process:

- **the abolition of roaming**, so from Lisbon one can speak with Karlovac at a price as if it were Oslo,
- **free travel**, so with just an ID card one can go from Karlovac to Stockholm or Uppsala without problems,
- **a common currency**, with which one immediately knows how much something is worth.

The EU is, he says, an **experiment that continues to this day**. Never in the history of the European continent have so many states been linked by essential elements of statehood, and that on a continent where for centuries "throats were cut" over political and religious differences. Today there is unrest and discontent, but they are legitimate and can be legitimately expressed.

sections.subtitle: Sedmogodišnji proračun EU-a: Europa po cijeni jedne kave dnevno
sections.screenshot_description: Picula objašnjava da europski proračun iznosi tek 1 posto zajedničkog BDP-a
sections.content:
Unija se, prema Piculi, našla u trenutku u kojem mora ozbiljno razmisliti **kako dalje**, nakon 80 godina europskog projekta. Kao ilustraciju tekućeg problema navodi pregovore o **sedmogodišnjem proračunu**. S jedne strane su države, među njima i Hrvatska, koje traže izdašan proračun kako bi se smanjivali razvojni dispariteti između razvijenijih i manje razvijenih. S druge su strane oni koji bi štedjeli jer proračun smatraju staromodnim i žele novac uložiti drugdje.

Predloženih **2.000 milijardi eura** za sedam godina, naglašava Picula, iznosi tek **1 posto zbrojenog BDP-a svih 27 država članica**. Netko je izračunao da je to, preračunato na plaće oko **450 milijuna građana EU-a**, **jedna kava dnevno**. Gost zato postavlja retoričko pitanje: je li projekt koji osobito malim državama jamči mir, prosperitet i prava na poslovanje i putovanje vrijedan jedne kave dnevno?

I što je alternativa? Da Hrvatska nije ušla u Uniju, kaže, bila bi **„u društvu s Vučićem“**, s disfunkcionalnom Bosnom i Hercegovinom i sličnim državama koje su zastale u demokratskoj tranziciji. Zato bi **1. srpnja 2013.**, dan ulaska Hrvatske u EU, uz šalu trebalo obilježavati gotovo kao vjerski praznik.

Voditelj se slaže, iako i sam zna kritizirati EU, te primjećuje da su mu gosti iz Bosne i Srbije pomalo zavidni, s razlogom kojeg ni sami Hrvati možda nisu svjesni. Picula podsjeća što je novinarima rekao na dan ulaska prije 13 godina: **pune koristi od Europske unije Hrvatska će imati tek kada svi njezini susjedi, na svakom centimetru vanjske granice, također budu u EU**, jer to znači da su riješeni mnogi problemi u tim državama i u odnosima s njima. To se neće dogoditi ni sutra ni prekosutra, ali tome treba težiti.
sections.subtitle_en: The seven-year EU budget: Europe for the price of one coffee a day
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula explains that the European budget amounts to only 1 percent of combined GDP
sections.content_en:
The Union, according to Picula, has found itself at a moment where it must seriously consider **how to proceed**, after 80 years of the European project. As an illustration of the current problem, he cites negotiations on the **seven-year budget**. On one side are states, among them Croatia, that seek a generous budget in order to reduce development disparities between the more developed and less developed. On the other side are those who would save because they consider the budget old-fashioned and want to invest money elsewhere.

The proposed **2,000 billion euros** over seven years, Picula emphasizes, amounts to only **1 percent of the combined GDP of all 27 member states**. Someone calculated that this, converted to the wages of about **450 million EU citizens**, is **one coffee a day**. The guest therefore asks a rhetorical question: is a project that especially guarantees peace, prosperity, and the rights to do business and travel to small states worth one coffee a day?

And what is the alternative? Had Croatia not entered the Union, he says, it would be **"in company with Vučić"**, with a dysfunctional Bosnia and Herzegovina and similar states that stalled in democratic transition. That is why **July 1, 2013**, the day of Croatia's entry into the EU, should jokingly be marked almost like a religious holiday.

The host agrees, although he himself knows how to criticize the EU, and observes that his guests from Bosnia and Serbia are somewhat envious, for a reason that Croats themselves might not even be aware of. Picula recalls what he told journalists on the day of entry 13 years ago: **Croatia will have the full benefits of the European Union only when all its neighbors, on every centimeter of the external border, are also in the EU**, because that means that many problems in those countries and in relations with them have been resolved. That will not happen tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, but one should strive toward that.

sections.subtitle: Putin kao ruski Justinijan: carski san o obnovi postsovjetskog prostora
sections.screenshot_description: Picula uspoređuje Putina s bizantskim carem Justinijanom
sections.content:
Na pitanje koliko je **ruska prijetnja Europi** stvarna, Picula odgovara da bi Putin, „da se ne zavaravamo“, htio biti uspješniji. Dugo je pripremao prodor preko Ukrajine prema onome što je smatrao vitalnom prijetnjom Ruskoj Federaciji. Treba znati, ističe, da je riječ o čovjeku koji je **raspad SSSR-a nazvao najvećom geopolitičkom katastrofom 20. stoljeća** i to nikada nije prebolio.

Demokratski eksperiment u vrijeme **Jeljcina** doveo je do velikih društvenih podjela, siromaštva i osjećaja izgubljenosti. Rusi su se u takvoj demokraciji osjećali vrlo loše, pa su priliku dali čovjeku koji im **jakom rukom i željeznom voljom** želi vratiti osjećaj dostojanstva i koji u Rusiji ima praktički nesputanu vlast.

Picula ga je, kaže, davno nazvao **„ruskim Justinijanom“**, po bizantskom caru koji je pokušao obnoviti Rimsko Carstvo prodorom na zapad. To je neko vrijeme išlo, ali je završilo gotovo katastrofom: carska blagajna je ispražnjena, zemlju je pogodila kuga, a nemiri su se nastavili. Putina, prema Piculi, ne karakterizira samo želja za dominacijom u Rusiji, nego i za **obnovom postsovjetskog prostora**.
sections.subtitle_en: Putin as a Russian Justinian: imperial dream of restoring the post-Soviet space
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula compares Putin to the Byzantine Emperor Justinian
sections.content_en:
When asked how real the **Russian threat to Europe** is, Picula answers that Putin, "lest we kid ourselves", would like to be more successful. He prepared the push through Ukraine for a long time toward what he considered a vital threat to the Russian Federation. One should know, he points out, that this is a man who **called the collapse of the USSR the greatest geopolitical catastrophe of the 20th century** and has never gotten over it.

The democratic experiment during **Yeltsin's** time led to great social divisions, poverty, and a sense of being lost. Russians felt very bad in such a democracy, so they gave an opportunity to a man who, with a **strong hand and iron will**, wants to restore their sense of dignity and who holds practically unfettered power in Russia.

Picula, he says, long ago dubbed him the **"Russian Justinian"**, after the Byzantine emperor who attempted to restore the Roman Empire by pushing westward. That worked for a while, but ended almost in catastrophe: the imperial treasury was emptied, the country was struck by plague, and unrest continued. Putin, according to Picula, is characterized not only by a desire for dominance in Russia, but also for the **restoration of the post-Soviet space**.

sections.subtitle: Ukrajina kao točka kristalizacije: od Majdana do sloma Merkeličine iluzije
sections.screenshot_description: Picula govori o slomu iluzije Angele Merkel i slabosti SAD-a nakon povlačenja iz Afganistana
sections.content:
Putinu se na putu, objašnjava Picula, ispriječila Europska unija, ali **ne kao vojna sila**. EU to nije i sumnja da će ikada postati. Unija je, međutim, svoj **model demokratizacije i suradnje** počela širiti na istok Europe i došla do Ukrajine, zbog čega se Putin osjetio ugroženim. Preko predsjednika **Janukoviča** pokušao je to zaustaviti, ali dogodila se **revolucija na Majdanu**. Zapad ju je, priznaje Picula, poticao, no najvažnije je da su Ukrajinci iskazali želju da **sami odlučuju u kojem smjeru žele ići**. Ukrajina je tako postala **točka kristalizacije** između ambicija ruskog vladara i Europske unije, koja je dotad prilično nesputano širila svoj model po kontinentu.

Pritom se dogodio i **slom iluzije Angele Merkel**, koja je vjerovala da će pojačanom trgovinom s Rusijom usput izvoziti i demokraciju. Putin je EU, kao i mnogi drugi, doživljavao kao prostor s kojim se isplati trgovati, ali mu se nije sviđala ideja širenja demokracije.

Na sigurnost Europe, dodaje gost, utjecala je i **slabost SAD-a**, osobito nakon odluke o **napuštanju Afganistana**. Putin je procijenio da se Amerikanci neće previše petljati ako napadne Ukrajinu, a Europska unija je bila beznadno podijeljena. To mu je bilo dovoljno da pokuša ostvariti svoj geopolitički san: **vratiti Rusiju u društvo najmoćnijih sila svijeta**.
sections.subtitle_en: Ukraine as a crystallization point: from Maidan to the collapse of Merkel's illusion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula speaks about the collapse of Angela Merkel's illusion and the weakness of the USA after the withdrawal from Afghanistan
sections.content_en:
In Putin's way, Picula explains, stood the European Union, but **not as a military force**. The EU is not that, and he doubts it ever will become one. The Union, however, began spreading its **model of democratization and cooperation** to the east of Europe and reached Ukraine, which made Putin feel threatened. Through President **Yanukovych** he tried to stop that, but the **revolution on the Maidan** occurred. The West, Picula admits, encouraged it, but the most important thing is that the Ukrainians expressed a desire to **decide for themselves in which direction they want to go**. Ukraine thus became a **crystallization point** between the ambitions of the Russian ruler and the European Union, which until then had rather unfettered spread its model across the continent.

At the same time, the **collapse of Angela Merkel's illusion** occurred as well, who believed that through increased trade with Russia she would also export democracy along the way. Putin, like many others, viewed the EU as an area worth trading with, but he did not like the idea of spreading democracy.

Europe's security, the guest adds, was also influenced by the **weakness of the USA**, especially after the decision to **abandon Afghanistan**. Putin assessed that the Americans would not meddle too much if he attacked Ukraine, and the European Union was hopelessly divided. That was enough for him to try to realize his geopolitical dream: **to return Russia to the company of the world's most powerful forces**.

sections.subtitle: Slovački ataše u Moskvi i Europa koja nije talionica naroda
sections.screenshot_description: Picula objašnjava da je vrijednost EU-a u tome što svatko može ostati Rumunj, Hrvat ili Šveđanin
sections.content:
Voditelj spominje vijest da je **Slovačka obnovila vojne diplomatske odnose s Rusijom**. Picula precizira da je Slovačka **poslala vojnog atašea u Moskvu** i navodi to kao primjer koliko je teško da Europska unija **govori jednim jezikom**.

EU, naglašava, **nije talionica naroda**, nije Sjedinjene Američke Države, i upravo u tome vidi njezinu vrijednost: svatko ulaskom u Uniju može ostati Rumunj, Hrvat, Šveđanin ili što god želi. Nacionalna pripadnost ne znači da se ne može sve bolje surađivati, a **prosperitet posljednjih 80 godina** dokazao je opravdanost takvog projekta.

No taj projekt ima i svoje **granice**. Svaka generacija političara i građana, zaključuje Picula, mora procijeniti što je moguće, koliko se Unija može dalje integrirati i gdje treba zastati i razmisliti kako dalje.
sections.subtitle_en: Slovak attaché in Moscow and a Europe that is not a melting pot of nations
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula explains that the value of the EU lies in the fact that everyone can remain Romanian, Croat, or Swede
sections.content_en:
The host mentions the news that **Slovakia has restored military diplomatic relations with Russia**. Picula clarifies that Slovakia **sent a military attaché to Moscow** and cites this as an example of how difficult it is for the European Union to **speak with one voice**.

The EU, he emphasizes, **is not a melting pot of nations**, it is not the United States of America, and precisely in that he sees its value: upon entering the Union everyone can remain Romanian, Croat, Swede, or whatever they wish. National affiliation does not mean that one cannot cooperate increasingly better, and the **prosperity of the last 80 years** proved the justification of such a project.

Yet that project also has its **limits**. Every generation of politicians and citizens, Picula concludes, must assess what is possible, how far the Union can integrate further, and where one should pause and consider how to proceed.
