sections.subtitle: Trumpov „dizelski dogovor“ s Moskvom i mir u Ukrajini koji se ne nazire
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pita Toninu Piculu što zapravo znači Trumpov dizelski dogovor s Rusijom
sections.content:
Nakon rasprave o Europskoj uniji i ruskoj prijetnji, voditelj podcasta prelazi na Washington. Povlači paralelu s Republikom Srpskom, gdje je Trumpova administracija skinula Milorada Dodika s crne liste, te ocjenjuje da je takozvani **dizelski dogovor** između Donalda Trumpa i Rusije na neki način vjetar u leđa Moskvi.

Voditelj podsjeća i na stanje na bojišnici. Mirovni dogovor Rusije i Ukrajine, kako kaže, još je daleko. Pregovori u Oslu nisu donijeli veći pomak, a žrtve i razaranja rastu na obje strane. Zaključuje da Trump ima „svoj način i svoj interes“ i od Tonina Picule traži objašnjenje što taj dogovor zapravo znači.
sections.subtitle_en: Trump's "diesel deal" with Moscow and peace in Ukraine nowhere in sight
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks Tonino Picula what Trump's diesel deal with Russia actually means
sections.content_en:
Following the discussion on the European Union and the Russian threat, the podcast host turns to Washington. He draws a parallel with Republika Srpska, where the Trump administration removed Milorad Dodik from the blacklist, and assesses that the so-called **diesel deal** between Donald Trump and Russia is in some way wind in the sails for Moscow.

The host also recalls the situation on the front line. A peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, as he says, is still far off. Negotiations in Oslo did not bring major progress, and casualties and destruction are mounting on both sides. He concludes that Trump has "his own way and his own interest" and asks Tonino Picula for an explanation of what that deal actually means.

sections.subtitle: Superizborni tjedan: svijet bi 4. studenog mogao izgledati drukčije
sections.screenshot_description: Tonino Picula nabraja izbore u Srbiji, Izraelu i SAD-u koji bi mogli promijeniti svjetski poredak
sections.content:
Prije odgovora o dizelu Picula upozorava na širi kontekst. Na dan snimanja, **27. listopada**, održavaju se još jedni važni izbori. Dva dana ranije pao je Aleksandar Vučić, a toga dana glasa se u **Izraelu**, gdje prema Piculinim riječima postoji mogućnost da vlast izgubi i Benjamin Netanyahu. Tjedan dana kasnije slijede **međuizbori u Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama**.

Picula zato smatra mogućim da svijet 4. studenog, nakon tih triju izbora, bude „konfiguriran nešto drugačije“ nego prije izbora u Srbiji. Dodaje i primjer iz Južne Amerike: u **Brazilu** je Lula, suprotno nekim očekivanjima, ponovno pobijedio, i to sina Bolsonara, kojeg su nazivali „tropskim Trumpom“.

Iz toga izvodi poruku: stvaraju se silnice koje se opiru trendovima što ih je ranije u razgovoru opisao kao tri megatrenda, a to su više sukoba uz slabljenje multilateralizma, fragmentacija političke scene i opće ubrzanje. Kako kaže, *„ne postoji unaprijed napisana povijest“*, ali postoje reakcije u društvu koje stignu brže nego što bi se očekivalo.
sections.subtitle_en: Super election week: the world could look different on November 4
sections.screenshot_description_en: Tonino Picula lists elections in Serbia, Israel, and the USA that could change the world order
sections.content_en:
Before answering about diesel, Picula warns of the broader context. On the day of recording, **October 27**, another set of important elections is being held. Two days earlier Aleksandar Vučić fell, and on that day voting is taking place in **Israel**, where according to Picula's words there is a possibility that Benjamin Netanyahu will lose power as well. A week later follow the **midterm elections in the United States of America**.

Picula therefore considers it possible that on November 4, after those three elections, the world will be "configured somewhat differently" than before the elections in Serbia. He also adds an example from South America: in **Brazil**, Lula, contrary to some expectations, won again, defeating the son of Bolsonaro, who was called the "tropical Trump".

From this he derives a message: lines of force are forming that resist the trends he described earlier in the conversation as three megatrends, which are more conflict along with the weakening of multilateralism, fragmentation of the political scene, and general acceleration. As he says, *"there is no pre-written history"*, but there are reactions in society that arrive faster than one would expect.

sections.subtitle: Dizel iz Rusije kao izraz očaja: napad na Iran i cijena galona goriva
sections.screenshot_description: Picula objašnjava kako je napad na Iran poremetio tržište energenata i natjerao Trumpa da traži dizel od Rusije
sections.content:
Odgovarajući na pitanje, Picula kaže da je dizel koji Trump „očajnički želi dobiti iz Rusije“ samo izraz očaja zbog posljedica politike koju je Trump sam skrivio. Ističe podatak koji, kako kaže, nije dovoljno poznat: **Sjedinjene Američke Države najveći su svjetski proizvođač nafte**, ispred svih drugih.

Uzrok vidi u napadu na **Iran**. Iranski režim opisuje kao krajnje antipatičan, autokratski i teokratski, režim koji ubija vlastite građane. Unatoč tome, smatra da je Trump svojim **nepripremljenim napadom** tom režimu u Teheranu produžio život, iako su ga vlastiti građani već počeli privoditi kraju. Napad je usto zakomplicirao stanje na svjetskom tržištu energenata toliko da Washington mora tražiti dizel od Rusije, koja je i sama postala parija moderne politike.

Motiv je, prema Piculi, domaći. Američki građani mjere „politički toplomjer“ prema Bijeloj kući ne po vanjskoj politici, nego po:

- cijenama u supermarketu,
- cijeni stanovanja,
- cijeni galona goriva.

Voditelj se nadovezuje podsjećanjem na „legendarno“ pitanje koliko košta tuce jaja u marketu i galon benzina, s čime se Picula u potpunosti slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Diesel from Russia as an expression of despair: attack on Iran and the price of a gallon of fuel
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula explains how the attack on Iran disrupted the energy market and forced Trump to seek diesel from Russia
sections.content_en:
Answering the question, Picula says that the diesel Trump "desperately wants to get from Russia" is only an expression of despair due to the consequences of a policy Trump himself brought about. He highlights a data point that, as he says, is not sufficiently known: **the United States of America is the world's largest producer of oil**, ahead of everyone else.

He sees the cause in the attack on **Iran**. He describes the Iranian regime as extremely unsympathetic, autocratic, and theocratic, a regime that kills its own citizens. Despite that, he believes that Trump, with his **unprepared attack**, prolonged the life of that regime in Tehran, even though its own citizens had already begun bringing it to an end. The attack additionally complicated the situation on the global energy market so much that Washington must seek diesel from Russia, which itself has become a pariah of modern politics.

The motive, according to Picula, is domestic. American citizens measure the "political thermometer" toward the White House not by foreign policy, but by:

- prices in the supermarket,
- the cost of housing,
- the price of a gallon of fuel.

The host follows up by recalling the "legendary" question of how much a dozen eggs in the supermarket and a gallon of gasoline cost, with which Picula completely agrees.

sections.subtitle: Od 11. rujna do sloma burze: „otac i majka“ Trumpova uspona
sections.screenshot_description: Tonino Picula opisuje 11. rujna i financijsku krizu kao događaje koji su otvorili put Trumpu
sections.content:
Picula Donalda Trumpa opisuje kao možda najbolju personifikaciju svijeta koji se počeo radikalno mijenjati. Početak te promjene smješta u **11. rujna 2001.**, u terorističke napade na blizance u New Yorku i na Pentagon u Washingtonu, nakon kojih se promijenila društvena atmosfera u SAD-u.

Drugi prijelomni događaj bio je **slom burze 2007. godine**, kada je Amerika praktički morala nacionalizirati gubitke golemih privatnih banaka. Ta dva događaja Picula naziva *„ocem i majkom“* Trumpova prvog dolaska na vlast 2016. godine.

Prema njegovoj analizi, frustracija i nezadovoljstvo američkim establishmentom, i demokratima i republikancima, otvorili su put čovjeku za kojeg nitko ne bi pretpostavio da će postati ikona frustriranih ljudi. Picula ga opisuje kao čovjeka koji je sam proživio puno bankrota i koji svojim ponašanjem „nije oličenje poštivanja obiteljskih vrijednosti“, a ipak je dvaput izabran za predsjednika SAD-a.

Bidenov povratak establishmenta 2020. godine, ocjenjuje Picula, nije ništa promijenio jer ta vrsta američkog establishmenta više ne pronalazi odgovore koji Amerikance zadovoljavaju. Tako je 2024. Trump ponovno pobijedio, a ostalo je, Piculinim riječima, *„the rest is history“*. Gost se nada da će Trump na međuizborima dobiti „ako ne crveni, onda žuti karton“, na što voditelj dodaje: „prvi žuti“.
sections.subtitle_en: From September 11 to the stock market crash: the "father and mother" of Trump's rise
sections.screenshot_description_en: Tonino Picula describes September 11 and the financial crisis as events that paved the way for Trump
sections.content_en:
Picula describes Donald Trump as perhaps the best personification of a world that began to change radically. He places the beginning of that change in **September 11, 2001**, in the terrorist attacks on the Twin Towers in New York and on the Pentagon in Washington, after which the social atmosphere in the USA changed.

The second turning point was the **stock market crash of 2007**, when America practically had to nationalize the losses of massive private banks. Picula calls those two events the *"father and mother"* of Trump's first coming to power in 2016.

According to his analysis, frustration and dissatisfaction with the American establishment, both Democrats and Republicans, paved the way for a man whom no one would have presumed would become an icon of frustrated people. Picula describes him as a man who himself lived through many bankruptcies and whose behavior "is not the epitome of respect for family values", and yet was twice elected president of the USA.

Biden's return of the establishment in 2020, Picula assesses, changed nothing because that kind of American establishment no longer finds answers that satisfy Americans. Thus in 2024 Trump won again, and what was left, in Picula's words, is *"the rest is history"*. The guest hopes that Trump will receive "if not a red, then a yellow card" in the midterms, to which the host adds: "a first yellow".

sections.subtitle: Ukrajina na dva fronta: Donbas na istoku, američka administracija na zapadu
sections.screenshot_description: Picula govori o Trumpovom pritisku na Zelenskog i poništenom paketu pomoći Ukrajini
sections.content:
Voditelj pita hoće li Trump dodatno smanjiti pomoć Ukrajini i još se više okrenuti Putinu. Picula smatra da je Trump već pojačao **prijetnje i pritiske prema Zelenskom**, i to kako bi se svidio Putinu i potaknuo ga da nešto napravi, odnosno da mu osobno izađe u susret uoči međuizbora (*midterm elections*).

Zato Ukrajina, kaže Picula, ima ozbiljan problem na fizičkoj bojišnici u Donbasu, ali se mora nositi i sa **„zapadnim frontom“**, a to je američka administracija.

Kao primjer navodi poništeni paket pomoći. Trump je toliko odustao od podrške Ukrajini da je poništio paket pomoći već dogovoren u Kongresu, koji je, kako navodi Picula, isposlovao pokojni Lindsey Graham, „veliki prijatelj Ukrajine, ali i prijatelj Trumpa“. Trump ga je, prema njegovim riječima, *„mrtav hladan“* odbio potpisati.

Takvu politiku Picula opisuje stihom iz pjesme: može „lavirati lijevo-desno“ bez čvrstog stava. Ipak, vjeruje da će nova većina u Kongresu morati i moći kontrolirati Trumpa do kraja mandata.
sections.subtitle_en: Ukraine on two fronts: Donbas in the east, American administration in the west
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula speaks about Trump's pressure on Zelenskyy and the canceled aid package to Ukraine
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether Trump will further reduce aid to Ukraine and turn even more toward Putin. Picula believes that Trump has already intensified **threats and pressure toward Zelenskyy**, specifically to please Putin and prompt him to do something, that is, to personally accommodate him ahead of the midterm elections (*midterm elections*).

That is why Ukraine, Picula says, has a serious problem on the physical battlefront in Donbas, but also has to deal with the **"western front"**, which is the American administration.

As an example he cites the canceled aid package. Trump gave up on supporting Ukraine to such an extent that he canceled an aid package already agreed upon in Congress, which, as Picula states, was brokered by the late Lindsey Graham, "a great friend of Ukraine, but also a friend of Trump". Trump, according to his words, *"cold-bloodedly"* refused to sign it.

Picula describes such a policy with a line from a song: one can "tack left and right" without a firm stance. Still, he believes that the new majority in Congress will have to and will be able to control Trump until the end of his term.

sections.subtitle: Najveća opasnost za hrvatsku demokraciju: građani koji odmahnu rukom
sections.screenshot_description: Tonino Picula upozorava da je ravnodušnost građana uvod u agoniju demokracije
sections.content:
Razgovor se zatim vraća u domaće dvorište. Voditelj ocjenjuje da u hrvatskoj politici ima previše bezobrazluka i ponašanja koje ne dolikuje političarima, posebno saborskim zastupnicima i zastupnicama, te smatra da je to daleko od vremena kad je Picula bio aktivan u domaćoj politici.

Picula odbija idealizirati prošlost. Ni njegovi dani, kaže, nisu bili idealni: i tada je u parlamentu bilo teških riječi, bilo je afera, a javnost je bila sumnjičava prema političarima. Ipak, primjećuje da s vremenom dolazi do **ukupne profanacije politike**, kojoj i sama politika doprinosi.

Najviše ga, međutim, ne brine način komunikacije u Saboru. *„Ja se bojim da građani ne odustanu od politike“*, kaže. Ako građani postanu ravnodušni, odmahnu rukom i kažu da su „svi isti i misle samo na sebe“, to je prema njemu uvod u **agoniju demokracije**.

Podsjeća da *republika* znači *javna stvar* te da javnost ne smije odustati od politike. Mora je moći kritizirati, ali politika se mora i obnavljati iz građanstva, koje mora biti dobro obrazovano i upućeno u mehanizme odlučivanja.
sections.subtitle_en: The greatest danger for Croatian democracy: citizens who wave their hands dismissively
sections.screenshot_description_en: Tonino Picula warns that citizens' indifference is a prelude to the agony of democracy
sections.content_en:
The conversation then returns to the domestic courtyard. The host assesses that in Croatian politics there is too much insolence and behavior unbecoming of politicians, especially members of parliament, and considers this to be far from the time when Picula was active in domestic politics.

Picula refuses to idealize the past. Even his days, he says, were not ideal: even then there were harsh words in parliament, there were scandals, and the public was suspicious of politicians. Nevertheless, he observes that over time an **overall profanation of politics** occurs, to which politics itself contributes.

Most of all, however, he is not worried by the manner of communication in the Sabor. *"I am afraid that citizens might give up on politics"*, he says. If citizens become indifferent, wave their hand dismissively, and say that "they are all the same and think only of themselves", according to him that is a prelude to the **agony of democracy**.

He recalls that *republic* means *public matter* and that the public must not give up on politics. It must be able to criticize it, but politics must also be renewed from the citizenry, which must be well-educated and knowledgeable about decision-making mechanisms.

sections.subtitle: Mobitel kao „pravi gazda“: tko danas odgaja mlade
sections.screenshot_description: Picula pokazuje mobitel kao „pravog gazdu“ suvremenog informiranja
sections.content:
Iz teme građanske odgovornosti Picula prelazi na obrazovanje. Pita tko danas odgaja i obrazuje mlade ljude, što su danas srednje škole i fakulteti i kakva se znanja u njima stječu.

Prema njegovoj ocjeni, **digitalna revolucija** snažno je oblikovala prostor politike. Informacije se danas prikupljaju preko mobitela, koje naziva *„pravim gazdom“*: ljudi gledaju u ekrane dok hodaju ulicom, pa čak i u društvu, u restoranu. Te su informacije, upozorava, često iskrivljene i plošne, ljudi ih prihvaćaju, a to ostavlja posljedice na kvalitetu političkog života.

Ipak, vidi i granicu tog procesa. Kao u Srbiji ili nekim drugim zemljama, društvo se u jednom trenutku okupi oko potrebe da se jasno kaže „ne“ ili jasno kaže „da“.
sections.subtitle_en: Mobile phone as the "real boss": who is educating the youth today
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula points to the mobile phone as the "real boss" of contemporary information
sections.content_en:
From the topic of civic responsibility, Picula moves on to education. He asks who today educates and raises young people, what secondary schools and universities are today, and what kind of knowledge is acquired in them.

According to his assessment, the **digital revolution** has strongly shaped the space of politics. Today information is gathered via mobile phones, which he calls the *"real boss"*: people look at screens while walking down the street, and even in company, in a restaurant. This information, he warns, is often distorted and flat, people accept it, and that leaves consequences on the quality of political life.

Nevertheless, he also sees a limit to that process. As in Serbia or some other countries, society at one moment gathers around the need to clearly say "no" or clearly say "yes".

sections.subtitle: Umjetna inteligencija: duh koji može pobjeći iz boce
sections.screenshot_description: Tonino Picula govori o Trumpovom odbijanju regulacije umjetne inteligencije zbog utrke s Kinom
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora voditelj se Piculi obraća kao sociologu i pita ga o **umjetnoj inteligenciji**. Prenosi i šalu jednog od prethodnih gostiju, prema kojem je nekim ljudima umjetna inteligencija prvi susret s inteligencijom uopće.

Picula odgovara vlastitom asocijacijom: pametni telefoni često su pametniji od onih koji ih drže u ruci, jer su ljudi pristali da im oni budu glavni izvor informacija i glavni kanal komunikacije umjesto razgovora sa susjedima, pa i s ukućanima. Prepričava i vic o čovjeku kojemu je nestalo interneta pa je morao razgovarati s ukućanima, nakon čega je zaključio: *„Fini neki ljudi.“*

Na to se, nastavlja Picula, nadovezala umjetna inteligencija, koja je prije pet do deset godina bila tema akademskih rasprava i stručnjaka, a danas je ozbiljan društveni i politički problem. Ključno pitanje, kao i toliko puta u povijesti tehnoloških revolucija, jest kako **uskladiti etiku i profit**. Riječ je o prostoru koji tek treba regulirati.

Picula opisuje dva tabora:

- **Protivnici regulacije** smatraju da se time guši nešto što mora ostati nesputano. Među njima su, prema Piculi, prije svega oni koji bi umjetnu inteligenciju koristili u vojne svrhe ili za stratešku prednost nad geopolitičkim suparnicima. Trump, kaže, ne želi ni čuti za regulaciju jer tvrdi da bi u tom slučaju Kinezi stekli nepovratnu prednost.
- **Zagovornici globalnih pravila**, među kojima su i neki od „očeva“ umjetne inteligencije, upozoravaju da je krajnje vrijeme da se lideri i biznis na globalnoj razini dogovore o pravilima igre, kako duh koji može pobjeći iz boce ne bi postao ozbiljna prijetnja čovjekovoj egzistenciji.

Picula priznaje da takva upozorenja ponekad zvuče zloguko i pretjerano, ali smatra da „ima tu nešto“. Problem vidi u tome što se dogovor traži u vremenu u kojem je multilateralni svijet, odnosno svijet organizacija u kojima se kolektivno dogovaralo, oslabljen. Umjetna inteligencija tako se kao šansa i kao prijetnja pojavljuje u nezgodnom trenutku, a razgovori o njezinoj budućnosti neće biti laki. Zaključuje da se stvari, nažalost, ne mogu vratiti unatrag, s čime se voditelj slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Artificial intelligence: a genie that can escape from the bottle
sections.screenshot_description_en: Tonino Picula speaks about Trump's refusal to regulate artificial intelligence due to the race with China
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the conversation, the host addresses Picula as a sociologist and asks him about **artificial intelligence**. He also relays a joke by one of the previous guests, according to whom for some people artificial intelligence is their first encounter with intelligence at all.

Picula responds with an association of his own: smartphones are often smarter than those who hold them in their hand, because people agreed to let them be their primary source of information and primary channel of communication instead of conversing with neighbors, and even with household members. He also recounts a joke about a man whose internet went out so he had to talk to his household members, after which he concluded: *"Quite nice people."*

Upon this, Picula continues, artificial intelligence followed, which five to ten years ago was a topic of academic discussions and experts, and today is a serious social and political problem. The key question, as so many times in the history of technological revolutions, is how to **reconcile ethics and profit**. This is an area that is yet to be regulated.

Picula describes two camps:

- **Opponents of regulation** believe that this stifles something that must remain unfettered. Among them, according to Picula, are primarily those who would use artificial intelligence for military purposes or for strategic advantage over geopolitical rivals. Trump, he says, does not even want to hear about regulation because he claims that in that case the Chinese would gain an irreversible advantage.
- **Advocates of global rules**, among whom are also some of the "fathers" of artificial intelligence, warn that it is high time for leaders and business to agree on the rules of the game at the global level, so that the genie that could escape from the bottle does not become a serious threat to human existence.

Picula admits that such warnings sometimes sound ominous and exaggerated, but believes that "there is something to it". He sees the problem in the fact that agreement is sought in a time when the multilateral world, that is, the world of organizations in which collective agreements were made, is weakened. Artificial intelligence thus appears as an opportunity and as a threat at an inconvenient moment, and conversations about its future will not be easy. He concludes that things, unfortunately, cannot be turned back, with which the host agrees.

sections.subtitle: „Srbija nije baba Roga“: bez kompleksa pred europskim putem susjeda
sections.screenshot_description: Picula poručuje da se Hrvatska ne treba bojati ubrzanog puta Srbije prema EU
sections.content:
Za kraj voditelj iznosi bojazan dijela hrvatske javnosti: hoće li Hrvatska postati „mala žrtva“ ako institucije u Bruxellesu požele ubrzati ulazak Srbije u Europsku uniju, pa Hrvatsku stave po strani.

Piculin odgovor počinje jasnom porukom: *„Mi ne smijemo imati komplekse. To je broj jedan.“* Hrvatska je, kaže, država i narod koji mora još puno raditi na sebi i koji ni izdaleka nije iskoristio svoje razvojne potencijale. Iako je dio suvereniteta predala Europskoj uniji, kao i mnogi drugi, ističe da Hrvatska nije i neće predati svoju sudbinu u tuđe ruke te da mora imati puno više samopouzdanja.

O Srbiji kaže da „nije baba Roga“. Smatra da će se još dugo baviti sama sobom, jer su problemi nastali zbog neriješene demokratske tranzicije iz devedesetih toliki da nove vlasti neće htjeti dodatno komplicirati ionako zamršene odnose u zemlji. Pred njima su elementarni zadaci:

- vladavina prava,
- suzbijanje korupcije,
- borba protiv mafije,
- sloboda tiska,
- gospodarska sfera.

Picula očekuje da će Europska unija procese u Srbiji pratiti sa zanimanjem. Ipak, ne vjeruje da će netko u Bruxellesu preko noći proglasiti Srbiju najboljim učenikom u razredu i omogućiti joj ono što nije omogućeno nikome drugom. Takav strah, zaključuje, govori o ljudima koji nemaju dovoljno povjerenja u Hrvatsku i njezine sposobnosti.

Voditelj se slaže i zahvaljuje gostu na razgovoru, a Tonino Picula uzvraća zahvalom.
sections.subtitle_en: "Serbia is not the Boogeyman": without complexes before the neighbor's European path
sections.screenshot_description_en: Picula says that Croatia should not fear Serbia's accelerated path toward the EU
sections.content_en:
In conclusion, the host expresses the fear of a part of the Croatian public: will Croatia become a "small victim" if institutions in Brussels wish to accelerate Serbia's entry into the European Union, thereby setting Croatia aside.

Picula's answer begins with a clear message: *"We must not have complexes. That is number one."* Croatia, he says, is a state and a nation that still needs to work hard on itself and has by no means utilized its development potentials. Although it surrendered part of its sovereignty to the European Union, like many others, he emphasizes that Croatia did not and will not surrender its fate into others' hands and must have much more self-confidence.

Regarding Serbia, he says that "it is not the Boogeyman". He believes that it will be preoccupied with itself for a long time to come, because the problems arising from the unresolved democratic transition of the nineties are so great that the new authorities will not want to further complicate already tangled relations in the country. Before them lie elementary tasks:

- the rule of law,
- combating corruption,
- the fight against the mafia,
- freedom of the press,
- the economic sphere.

Picula expects that the European Union will follow processes in Serbia with interest. Still, he does not believe that someone in Brussels will overnight proclaim Serbia the best pupil in class and enable it to have what has not been enabled to anyone else. Such fear, he concludes, speaks of people who do not have enough confidence in Croatia and its capabilities.

The host agrees and thanks the guest for the conversation, and Tonino Picula returns the thanks.
